course.title: Painting and Decorating
course.tagline: Paint walls, rooms and homes with a clean, professional finish.

days.title: Prepare a Room for Painting
days.goal: Get a room ready so paint goes on clean walls, not on furniture.

video.title: How to Prepare a Room for Painting

steps: Move furniture to the middle and cover it with dust sheets.
Take down curtains, pictures and light switch covers.
Fill holes and cracks with filler and let it dry.
Wash the walls with sugar soap (a cleaner that removes grease) and let them dry.
days.task: Prepare one room fully: covered, filled and washed.
days.challenge: Prepare a room in under one hour.

quiz.q: What should you do first before painting a room?
options: Move and cover furniture, then fill and wash the walls
quiz.explain: Preparation protects furniture and gives paint a clean surface to stick to.

quiz.q: What is sugar soap used for?
options: Cleaning walls of grease before painting
quiz.explain: Sugar soap removes grease and dirt so paint sticks properly.

quiz.q: Why fill holes before painting?
options: So the finished wall is smooth
quiz.explain: Unfilled holes show through paint and spoil the finish.

days.title: Tools: Rollers, Brushes and Trays
days.goal: Know the painting tools and what each one does.

video.title: How to Prepare a Room for Painting

steps: Lay out rollers, brushes, a tray, a roller pole and masking tape.
Learn that rollers cover big areas fast and brushes cut in edges.
Pick the right roller sleeve (the fluffy cover) for smooth or rough walls.
Wash new brushes before first use to remove loose hairs.
days.task: Set up a painting kit with every tool named.
days.challenge: Pick the right roller for a smooth wall and a rough wall.

days.title: Masking and Cutting In
days.goal: Mask edges and paint clean lines where walls meet ceilings.

video.title: How to Prepare a Room for Painting

steps: Masking tape is tape that protects edges from paint.
Press tape along skirting boards, ceilings and door frames.
Cut in means painting the edges with a brush first.
Paint a straight line along the ceiling with a steady hand.
days.task: Cut in one wall with a clean straight line at the ceiling.
days.challenge: Cut in a whole room with no wobbly lines.

days.title: Paint a Room Step by Step
days.goal: Paint a full room in the right order.
steps: Paint the ceiling first, then the walls, then the woodwork.
Cut in the edges, then roll the middle.
Work in small sections and keep a wet edge (paint into paint that is still wet).
Let the first coat dry fully before the second.
days.task: Paint one room with two coats.
days.challenge: Paint a room with no roller marks showing.

quiz.q: What is a roller sleeve?
options: The fluffy cover that holds paint on a roller
quiz.explain: The sleeve holds the paint and rolls it onto the wall.

quiz.q: What is a roller best for?
quiz.explain: Rollers cover large areas quickly; brushes do the edges.

quiz.q: What does cutting in mean?
options: Painting edges with a brush before rolling
quiz.explain: Cutting in paints the edges a roller cannot reach.

days.title: Roller Technique
days.goal: Roll paint evenly with no streaks or roller marks.
steps: Load the roller evenly: roll it in the tray, not too much paint.
Roll in a W shape, then fill it in.
Do not press hard: let the roller do the work.
Roll the final pass in one direction for an even finish.
days.task: Roll one wall with no streaks or lines.
days.challenge: Roll a wall so smooth you cannot see where you started.

days.title: Two Coats and Drying Times
days.goal: Know why two coats matter and how long to wait between them.
steps: One coat often looks patchy when it dries.
Wait the time on the tin before the second coat.
Check the paint is dry to the touch, not just looks dry.
Ventilate the room so paint dries evenly.
days.task: Paint a wall with two coats and record the drying times.
days.challenge: Get full coverage with two thin coats, not one thick one.

days.title: Project: Paint One Wall
days.goal: Paint one wall from prep to finish with clean edges.
steps: Fill and sand any holes, then wash the wall.
Mask the edges and cut in with a brush.
Roll two coats, letting the first dry.
Remove the tape while the last coat is still slightly wet.

quiz.q: In what order do you paint a room?
quiz.explain: Top to bottom means drips fall on unpainted surfaces below.

quiz.q: What is a wet edge?
options: Painting into paint that is still wet so no lines show
quiz.explain: Keeping a wet edge stops lines where one section meets the next.

quiz.q: Why wait between coats?
options: So the first coat dries fully and the second sticks well
quiz.explain: Painting too soon can lift the first coat and spoil the finish.

days.title: Paint a Wall Smoothly
days.goal: Get a smooth finish with no brush marks or bubbles.
steps: Use a good quality roller sleeve for smooth walls.
Do not overload the roller with paint.
Roll slowly and evenly, keeping a wet edge.
Fix bubbles by rolling over them gently before they dry.

days.challenge: Fix a bubbled patch without repainting the whole wall.

days.title: Paint an Apartment
days.goal: Plan and paint a whole small apartment room by room.

video.title: How to Paint a Wall Smoothly

steps: List every room and the paint each needs.
Work out how much paint to buy: one litre covers about 10 square metres.
Paint one room at a time, top to bottom.

quiz.q: How do you avoid roller marks?
options: Load evenly, roll in a W and finish in one direction
quiz.explain: Even loading and a final pass in one direction leaves no marks.

quiz.q: What causes paint bubbles?
options: Too much paint or a hot wall
quiz.explain: Too much paint or heat traps air and makes bubbles.

quiz.q: How do you fix a bubble?
options: Roll over it gently before it dries
quiz.explain: Gentle rolling while wet smooths bubbles away.

days.title: Fix Drips and Runs
days.goal: Fix paint drips before they dry hard.

video.title: How to Choose a Roller Nap and Brush

steps: Catch drips while wet: brush them out gently.
If a drip dries, sand it flat and repaint that spot.

Check your work in good light before you pack up.

quiz.q: Which brush suits water-based paint?
quiz.explain: Synthetic brushes hold their shape in water-based paint.

quiz.q: Why clean brushes after use?
options: So they stay soft and last for years
quiz.explain: Dried paint ruins brushes; clean ones last for many jobs.

quiz.q: How do you match texture when patching a wall?
options: Dab the filler with a sponge to copy the pattern

quiz.q: Why remove loose bits before patching?

capstone.title: Paint a Real Room
capstone.brief: Paint a real room from preparation to finish — ceiling, walls and woodwork, two coats, tidy handover — and present it with the quote and colours used.
checks: Room fully prepared: covered, filled, washed
Two coats everywhere with even coverage
Clean edges with no paint on ceilings or floors
No drips, runs or missed spots
Room clean and tidy on handover
Quote, colours and care notes presented
deliverables: Quote with paint, time and price
List of colours and paint used
